prompt: Look at `SemanticSignatureElement::getNeverWritesMask` in llvm/include/llvm/Frontend/HLSL/SemanticSignatures.h. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: It is not. The planted change masks the complement of the usage mask down to the element's own declared columns: it returns `~UsageMask & getDeclaredMask()` instead of `~UsageMask & 0xF`, so NeverWrites now reports only the declared components the shader leaves alone, and every component outside the element's declared columns comes out as 0, which in this field means written. The intended rule is in llvm/docs/DirectX/SemanticSignatures.md, section Derived Container Fields (added 2026-07-22 in #206804): for outputs `NeverWrites = ~UsageMask & 0xF`, and the output mask includes components outside the declared mask. Consequence: an output element that does not cover the whole register row, say `float A : A` at one column of a shared row, now claims the three components it never declared are written, so OSG1 and PSV0 tell a later stage those components carry a value, and the container disagrees with the one DXC writes. An element declaring all four columns at column 0 has a declared mask of 0xF, so the two agree there and the change is invisible in the common case. The expectation that pinned the rule (MetadataToElementDerivedMasks in llvm/unittests/Frontend/HLSLSemanticSignatureMetadataTest.cpp) was changed with it, so it is not the intent; the container tests under llvm/test/CodeGen/DirectX/ContainerData/ were left alone and still expect the documented ExclusiveMask of 14 for the one-column output A and 9 for B, so naming those is as good as naming the document.
